kind: Source-informed local protocol; not external preregistration
question: Does interrupted LinEra compaction preserve readability of unrelated surviving objects after restart while previously forgotten lineage stays unreadable?
basis: Pinned rotate commits re-encrypted rows before saving fresh key state; upstream selected test covers completed rotation, not this interruption. This motivates a bounded availability check, not a cryptographic attack claim.
cases: process exit at rotate state-save entry, after database commit and before fresh state file publication
fixture: Two sources, one derivative of forgotten source, one derivative of retained source; synthetic canary strings. Single writer, fresh isolated temporary directory per case.
measurement: Exact read outcomes for each object after reopen
Outcome exception class; do not collapse invalid authentication into readable false silently
Original source hashes before and after
Subprocess exit and injected boundary records
expectations: Complete controls should retain unrelated plaintext and reject forgotten lineage. Interrupted rotate may lose survivor readability; preserve any contrary result.
instrumentation: Separate copied source; intercept instance state-save boundary after setup and call os._exit in subprocess. No upstream source edits; no model/remote API/physical-power-loss simulation.
limits: Process exit at an instrumented boundary is not arbitrary filesystem power loss.
Availability loss is distinct from recovery of forgotten data or breaking the LC-FS theorem.
No repair comparator or new algorithm claimed.
Only selected LineageStore compaction, not vector index or mem0 end-to-end.
execution_gate: Inspect/use an existing isolated cryptography runtime or create a small separate pinned environment; shared Python lacks cryptography. Do not execute model acquisition or paper-wide scripts.
